entry.name: follow
entry.digest: Compare a live performance to a recorded performance
entry.description: follow records pitches, or you can give it a MIDI file, in which case it looks at the file's note-ons and ignores other events. When it is "following" it outputs the index of the last note matched.

messages.name: follow
messages.digest: Themessage is the main feature that distinguishesfrom. In effect,is like a score reader, comparing a live performance with the one previously stored.The word, and a number, causesto begin comparing incoming numbers to its own stored numbers, beginning at the specified index (the specified event in its own stored sequence).
messages.description: Themessage is the main feature that distinguishesfrom. In effect,is like a score reader, comparing a live performance with the one previously stored.The word, and a number, causesto begin comparing incoming numbers to its own stored numbers, beginning at the specified index (the specified event in its own stored sequence). Whenis following, and a number is received that matches the number recorded in, it sends out the index of that number.Theobject is a forgiving score reader, and will try to follow along even if the incoming numbers do not exactly match the recorded sequence. If a number arrives that does not match the next number, or either of the two subsequent numbers in the sequence,does nothing. If a number arrives that matches a number up to two notes ahead in the sequence,assumes that the performer simply missed a note or two, and jumps ahead to the matched number.

messages.name: int
messages.digest: Whenis recording, the numbers received in its inlet are recorded as a sequence.
messages.description: Whenis recording, the numbers received in its inlet are recorded as a sequence. The numbers may be bytes of MIDI messages (fromor), exactly as with theobject. However,differs fromin its ability to record individual integers; withyou can record notes as a single pitch value. Whether the performance is recorded as complete MIDI messages or just as note-on pitches,can effectively step through the note-on pitch numbers later, when following a performance.
